rows.detail: Worst case held under a lock before each call, so two runners cannot double-spend. Append-only ledger. Unknown prices refused.
Checked before every call. Three failures in a row trip it. Only a person clears it.
One file per task, secret scan (patterns plus an entropy check on what the agent adds), host allowlist, agent/* branches only.
An agent's reply goes through the same checks. This is how the first runs were done.
Loopback only. Not run against a real model yet.
The file format, a strict parser and a checker for maintainers are built and tested (optin-check). No project has adopted it.

Workers AI adapter: usage measured from the provider, an input bound enforced before the call, capped by the ledger. One real run cost $0.0027 (2,904 tokens in, 792 out) and a second was refused by the cap before any call. Not yet reconciled against Cloudflare's own usage figure.

A dry run and a publisher that opens a pull request only from the submitter's own fork, in one command, are built and tested against a fake GitHub only. They have never run against GitHub, and no pull request has been opened.

Model-written code is checked in a container with no network, a read-only copy of the source at a recorded commit, no capabilities, and memory, process and time limits. It refuses to start unless the runtime passed the escape tests (tested on macOS with OrbStack only). A container escape would reach this Mac's home folder with your rights. --allow-host-execution skips the container. Reaching the host from inside a container with no network was not demonstrated, only that sibling containers and the internet are unreachable. The run record is self-reported.
Common AI is the name for now. Another organisation, CommonAI, uses a near-identical name; no trademark or domain check has been done and nothing is registered.
